findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public IP/DNS endpoint reachable from outside the VPC. A database holding application data should never be internet-addressable; reachability is then governed only by a security group rule, which is a single line of defence.

storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS storage volume, its snapshots, and automated backups unencrypted at rest, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a snapshot copy can read the data.

The user_data bootstrap script writes the live database password (${var.password}), username, and endpoint in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc and into the instance user data itself, which is readable via the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF on the host. Secrets should be delivered from a secrets manager or IAM-authenticated role, not baked into launch scripts.

This policy attached to the app role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance full control of storage, compute, and databases across the account. Combined with the internet-facing web application that assumes this role, any compromise of the host yields unrestricted account-wide access and a direct privilege-escalation path.

The database security group permits all protocols and all ports (protocol = "-1", 0-0) to 0.0.0.0/0. Combined with the publicly accessible instance, this removes any egress restriction that would otherwise limit data exfiltration from a compromised database host.
